title: Coffee and walnut traybake
subtitle: British coffee cake baked flat with coffee buttercream
excerpt: Coffee and walnut traybake is a British classic baked in a rectangular tin and cut into squares, making it straightforward to transport and serve. The coffee sponge has a fine, even crumb and a gentle bitterness balanced by the coffee buttercream. Use instant espresso powder dissolved in a small amount of boiling water for the clearest coffee flavour.
sourceNotes: British coffee cake tradition (documented in various 20th-century household baking manuals, public domain). Mary Berry, various publicly documented traditional British cake recipes.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uniced squares for up to 2 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the sponge 1 day ahead and ice on the day of serving.

baking.decoratingTechnique: Coffee buttercream spread with palette knife, walnut halves to decorate

recipeTools.notes: 30 x 20 cm tin, greased and lined.

glossaryTerms.definition: Beating softened butter and sugar together until the mixture is pale, light, and fluffy before adding eggs and flour. The process incorporates air into the fat, which helps the cake rise and gives a fine, even crumb. The butter must be genuinely soft (not melted) for the method to work. Under-creamed butter and sugar produces a dense, heavy sponge.

A frosting made by beating together softened butter and icing sugar until smooth and spreadable. The ratio is typically 1 part butter to 2 parts icing sugar by weight. Flavourings (here, dissolved instant coffee) are added once the butter and sugar are combined. Buttercream stiffens in the refrigerator and softens at room temperature.

content.text: Coffee and walnut traybake is a
sponge baked in a single flat tin. You get 16 even squares with a coffee sponge, a coffee
top, and a walnut half on each square. The traybake format is easier to serve than a layered cake and holds up well for a day or two after icing.

content.text: Heat the oven to 180 degrees Celsius (conventional). Grease and line the base and sides of a 30 x 20 cm rectangular baking tin.

Beat the softened butter and caster sugar together for 4 to 5 minutes until pale and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. If the batter looks like it is splitting, add a tablespoon of the flour.
Fold in the self-raising flour and baking powder with a large spatula until just combined. Stir in the cooled coffee mixture and the chopped walnuts.

Spoon into the prepared tin and level the surface. Bake for 28 to 32 minutes until the sponge has pulled away from the sides, springs back when pressed in the centre, and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a cooling rack and leave until completely cold before icing.

Beat the softened butter until smooth, then add the sifted icing sugar in two batches, beating on low speed to combine before increasing to medium. Add the cooled coffee mixture and beat for 1 to 2 minutes until the buttercream is light and creamy.

Place the cold sponge on a board. Spread the buttercream evenly over the top with a palette knife, taking it right to the edges. Place a walnut half in the centre of each intended square. Cut into 16 squares with a sharp knife, cleaning the blade between cuts.

attrs.problem: Sponge is dense rather than light
attrs.fix: Beat the butter and sugar for a full 4 to 5 minutes until the mixture is noticeably pale and has increased in volume. Undermixing at this stage is the most common reason for a heavy sponge.

attrs.problem: Buttercream is too stiff to spread
attrs.avoid: Avoid making the buttercream when the butter is cold from the refrigerator.
attrs.fix: Leave the butter at room temperature for at least 1 hour before beating. If the buttercream is already made and is too stiff, beat in 1 teaspoon of warm water at a time until it loosens to a spreadable consistency.

attrs.avoid: Avoid using filter coffee or brewed espresso in place of instant espresso powder.
attrs.fix: Instant coffee dissolved in a very small amount of hot water gives a concentrated, clean coffee flavour that reads clearly through butter and sugar. Add an extra half teaspoon of instant coffee to both the sponge and buttercream if a stronger result is wanted.
